Dein Schreibtisch im Revier steht noch d: Your desk at the station is still there. Someone cleared it and then never carried it away. In the drawer lies a pencil stub you wrote the first file with. When you touch it, the station is loud and young again for a breath, and you were only a person with a lantern.
Die Kellertür des Pfandhauses in der Ash: The cellar door of the pawnshop in Ashgrove Lane is nailed shut. This is where it all began: a missing man, a cellar, a voice in the dark. Today you no longer hear the voice. You understand now what it said back then.
Die Turmuhr geht seit deiner Abreise gen: Since you left, the tower clock runs slow by exactly as many minutes as the Sequences you have climbed. The clockmaker swears she adjusted nothing. You lay your hand on the works, and the hands jump to the right time.
Hinter Nells Stand liegt der Kessel, in: Behind Nell's stall lies the kettle you brewed your first potion in, dented and cold. Back then one sip made your hands shake. Today you could silence the whole market with a thought. You don't.
Am Brunnen klebt dein Steckbrief, ausgeb: Your wanted poster is pasted on the well, faded, with a face that no longer quite looks like you. Underneath, someone has written in chalk: "Don't touch. He comes back." Three candles burn beside it.
Hier am Kai hast du zum ersten Mal mit d: Here on the quay you first looked with spirit sight and feared what you saw. The water is the same. The things in it now shrink back from you until the bay is as empty as a swept floor.
Auf dem Bahnsteig liegt noch der Abdruck: On the platform the imprint of your suitcase is still in the soot, as if no one had swept it away. Back then you came as a wanted person, with a ticket and nothing else. The telegraphist looks up, recognises you and forgets to finish tapping the telegram.
Im Kahn hängt noch deine Decke über der: Your blanket still hangs over the bunk in the barge. Tinder never took it down. A note in her hand lies on the table: "If you come back: the kettle is still warm. If you don't: same."
Im Kahn ist deine Pritsche abgezogen, di: In the barge your bunk has been stripped, the blanket folded at its foot. Tinder hasn't been here since you took office. On the table lies a note in her hand, already yellowed: "I still won't sell you oil." Below it, in different ink and added later: "The kettle is warm anyway."
Der Kahn liegt verlassen am Kai. Seit du: The barge lies abandoned at the quay. Since you fled to sea with Kit and Tinder, no one has set foot in it. Your blanket still hangs over the bunk, stiff with salt. On the table stands an empty oil can with a note in Tinder's hand: "If you come back: we're at sea. If you don't: same."
Der Stand, an dem man dich verraten hat: The stall where you were betrayed
An diesem Stand hat dich jemand an die G: At this stall someone sold you to the Grey Scouts for a sack of salt. The stall is empty, the sign unscrewed. People give it a wide berth, as if the ground were hot.
Das Leuchtfeuer brennt nicht mehr so, wi: The beacon no longer burns the way it did back then. It has become an ordinary light, for ships, not for souls. On the steps lie shells, candle stubs and a note: "Thank you."
Das Leuchtfeuer brennt noch wie damals,: The Beacon still burns as it did back then, and Brandt stands at the lens above. When you look up the steps, the fire turns away, for the first time in three hundred years, and searches elsewhere. On the steps lie shells and a note: "Get us out of here."
Das Leuchtfeuer erkennt dich, bevor du d: The Beacon recognises you before you open the door. It lies down before you like a dog before its master, and the tablets on the walls rattle. On the steps lie no shells but petitions, addressed to the Light Master. To you.
Dein Name im Hörsaal: Your name in the lecture hall
Auf der Tafel im Hörsaal steht dein Name: Your name is on the blackboard in the lecture hall, half wiped away, and beneath it a question in Wyle's hand: "How much of a person remains at Sequence 3?" No one has answered it. You pick up the chalk and lower it again.
Im Lichtamt steht deine Akte im Regal, d: Your file stands on the shelf in the Office of Light, thick as a hymnal. A new label is stuck on its spine: "Closed. Not enforceable." Below, smaller: "God help us."
Am Endbahnhof steht der Bahnsteig, an de: At the terminus is the platform where you followed Starling onto the train going up. The rails now end in a wall of lime. Children have painted on it: a train, a figure of light falling down, and the same figure getting up again.
Im Speisewagen steht dein Becher noch im: In the dining car your mug still stands on the shelf, with a chalk mark for every day you were gone. At some point Whistle stopped counting and drew a circle instead.
Die Drehscheibe im Runddepot dreht sich,: When you step onto it, the turntable in the roundhouse turns, without any steam, once around, and stops with its rail pointing upward. The workers take off their caps.
Am letzten Bahnsteig hast du zum ersten: On the last platform you first heard of the Old One. The voice that came from the rails back then is silent. Perhaps it is afraid of you. Perhaps it is only waiting.
Auf dem Kalkmarkt verkauft jemand kleine: At the lime market someone is selling little lime figures: a shape in your coat with a halo of soot. "Lucky charms," says the trader without looking at you. "Against overseers."
Im Teesaal ist dein Tisch am Fenster imm: In the tea room your table by the window is always free. Mabel sets a cup on it every evening that nobody drinks. Today you drink it. It is cold and still tastes of arriving.
Miss Pimm lässt den Stempel fallen. „Sie: Miss Pimm drops her stamp. "You …" She composes herself. "The Inspector said you would come back. I didn't believe her. But your chair is still here. Nobody wanted to take it."
Halloway weicht hinter den Tresen zurück: Halloway backs behind the counter until the shelf rattles. "I nailed the cellar shut. I swear I nailed it shut."
Constable Price legt die Hand an den Knü: Constable Price puts his hand to his truncheon, looks you in the eye and takes it away again. "I have orders to arrest you," he says quietly. "I also have children."
Wick pfeift durch die Zähne. „Die ganze: Wick whistles through his teeth. "The whole alley is talking about you. Half are praying, the other half are packing."
Der blinde Ned hebt den Kopf, bevor du e: Blind Ned lifts his head before you say anything. "You sound different. Like a bell you hear in your belly instead of your ear."
Mr. Quill schreibt nicht weiter. „Ich ha: Mr. Quill stops writing. "I wrote a column about you. The publisher burned it. He said he didn't want you to read it."
Pater Ambrose bekreuzigt sich, zögert un: Father Ambrose crosses himself, hesitates, and then doesn't know whether he did it against you or for you.
Maud stellt dir ein Glas hin und tritt e: Maud sets a glass in front of you and steps back. "On the house. Everything's on the house. Please don't stay too long."
Nell lacht, zu laut. „Sieh an, mein best: Nell laughs, too loudly. "Look who it is, my best customer. I hear you don't need ingredients any more. You've become one."
Kittering verbeugt sich so tief, dass se: Kittering bows so low that his hat falls off. "For you: everything at cost. For you: everything free, if you wish. Do you wish it?"
Ezra am Nordtor hält das Tor auf, ohne d: Ezra at the North Gate holds the gate open before you ask. "The watch said we should stop you. I asked them with what."
Meisterin Brass sieht auf ihre Taschenuh: Master Brass looks at her pocket watch, then at you. "Since you arrived, it keeps proper time. It never did before."
Odile Crane schiebt dir ein Pfandbuch hi: Odile Crane pushes a pawn ledger towards you. "You're in there. As a pledge. Someone pawned you for a candle. I couldn't bring myself to strike it out."
Abel Druce sieht von seinem Fahrplan auf: Abel Druce looks up from his timetable and silently crosses out a line. "Special train. Every train stops for you now."
Hesper Quell lässt das Salz durch die Fi: Hesper Quell lets the salt run through her fingers. "They say the moor goes quiet where you walk. I didn't believe it. Listen." It is quiet.
Ottilie Fenn misst dich mit den Augen un: Ottilie Fenn measures you with her eyes and puts the tape away. "Nothing I can sew fits you any more. Not because of the size."
Ottilie Brack pulls her headscarf lower. "The Grey Scouts issued a decree: whoever sees you should get out of your way. First decree everyone actually follows."
Der Pedell schließt die Tür hinter dir,: The beadle closes the door behind you very softly, as if it might break. "The Magistra says you have become an exam question."
Mutter Sedge nimmt deine Hand und lässt: Mother Sedge takes your hand and lets go at once, as if she had burned herself. "Child. What have they made of you? No. What have you made of yourself?"
Magistra Wyle legt die Brille ab. „Ich h: Magistra Wyle takes off her glasses. "I lost a bet. I said no one comes back from up there."
Agathe Mulch sieht dich an wie ein Maß,: Agathe Mulch looks at you like a measurement that doesn't fit. "I have no coffin for you. I don't think you need one any more."
Corvin Tallow hält die Feder über dem Pa: Corvin Tallow holds his pen over the paper and writes nothing. "The office has instructed me not to record your arrival. They say you read along."
Der Grauspäher tritt beiseite und senkt: The Grey Scout steps aside and lowers his gaze. Behind his mask you hear him forget to breathe.
Pfiff lässt den Becher fallen. Er fängt: Whistle drops his mug. He catches it before it hits the floor and laughs as though he had caught you. "You came down. Of your own accord. Nobody has ever done that."
Nellie Swarth starrt dich an, dann den H: Nellie Swarth stares at you, then at the sky, then at you again. "You were up there. You were really up there. What's it like? No. Don't tell me."
Dr. Huxford legt das Stethoskop weg, bev: Dr. Huxford sets the stethoscope aside before he even touches you. "I can hear your heart from here. It no longer quite beats to this rhythm."
Esther Brindle zählt die Lohntüten zweim: Esther Brindle counts the pay packets twice and pushes one towards you. "The shift took a collection. In case you came back. In case you needed something. What do you need?"
Jonas Pelham tritt vom Stand zurück und: Jonas Pelham steps back from the stall and raises his hands as if you were an overseer. Then he realises you are worse, and lets them drop.
Adaine Quarrell nickt dir zu wie einem a: Adaine Quarrell nods to you like an old creditor. "The quarry steps stopped slipping while you were up there. Today they slip again. Only away from you."
Mabel Caskett stellt dir eine Tasse hin,: Mabel Caskett sets a cup in front of you with both hands so it won't shake. "The table by the window is free. It was always free."
Oren Fallowby wischt sich die Hände an d: Oren Fallowby wipes his hands on his apron again and again. "The depot is running. Everything is running. You needn't touch anything. Please don't touch anything."
Willa Trentfold umarmt dich, bevor sie e: Willa Trentfold hugs you before she can think better of it, then steps back startled. "You're warm. Like a stove. Like an engine."
Perrin Gallowmere zieht den Hut. „Der le: Perrin Gallowmere raises his hat. "The last platform hasn't seen a train since you left. I think it's waiting for your return journey."
Ein kleiner Schrein aus Kisten und Kerze: A small shrine of crates and candles. Inside stands a crude figure in your coat, with coins, bread and a child's shoe laid before it. No one is in sight, but the wax is still warm.
Eine Schale voller Münzen und Zettel. Au: A bowl full of coins and notes. One says: "Please don't take my brother." Another: "Please take my landlord."
Jemand hat aus Schwellen und Kalk einen: Someone has built an altar of sleepers and lime, exactly where the train going up departed. On it lie tickets with no destination.
Dein Steckbrief, ein Dutzend Mal. Auf je: Your wanted poster, a dozen times over. The face has been scratched out on every one. Not out of hatred, says a note beside them: "You shouldn't look at it. It looks back."
Pater Ambrose senkt die Stimme. „Seit du: Father Ambrose lowers his voice. "Since you left, something screams in the crypt. At night, always at three. I prayed, I burned incense, I had the door walled up. It screams through the wall. You are the only thing in this city it might be afraid of."
Hinter der vermauerten Tür kauert ein Ec: Behind the walled-up door crouches an echo that has sunk its teeth into an old grave. It screams at you, then recognises you and falls silent mid-note. You tell it that it may go. It goes. For the first time in months the crypt is quiet.
Nell schiebt dir ein Fläschchen hin: „Ha: Nell pushes a vial towards you: "Hair of the Demigod, genuine, blessed". "Someone in the harbour warehouse is bottling this stuff and selling it to people who are afraid of you. Some drink it. Two are in hospital. I'm not touching it. You can."
Zwischen den Kisten stehen Hunderte Fläs: Between the crates stand hundreds of vials of grey brew with a label bearing your face. The bottler fled long ago when he heard who was coming. You smash the stock, crate by crate. On the last label you write: "Do not drink."
Mutter Sedge hält dich am Ärmel fest. „D: Mother Sedge holds you by the sleeve. "The moor has been taking children since you left. Not many. One a month. They go to the peat cutting at night and don't come back. We hear them singing. Go there. Please."
Unter dem Torf singt etwas mit Kindersti: Beneath the peat something sings with children's voices. When you kneel, it stops. You dig with your hands, and the peat gives way like cloth. Three children sleep beneath it, cold but alive. The moor lets them go as though it had only been keeping them for you.
Hesper wischt sich die Hände an der Schü: Hesper wipes her hands on her apron. "The brine in the Buoy Harbour talks. It says names. Whoever hears their name is standing in the water the next morning and doesn't know how they got there. My nephew heard his name yesterday."
Die Lake flüstert, und dann flüstert sie: The brine whispers, and then it whispers your name. You answer. Not with words. The water draws back as if it had burned itself, and on the bottom lies a rusted bell that no one will ever ring again.
Esther Brindle legt den Finger auf drei: Esther Brindle lays her finger on three names. "Buried. In the quarry, under the steps. The overseers say nothing can be done. The overseers always say that. We can still hear them knocking."
Du legst die Hand auf den Kalk. Er gibt: You lay your hand on the lime. It yields, stone by stone, as though the mountain remembered something it owed you. Three men crawl into the light, grey as statues. One asks whether he is dead now. You say: not yet.
Mabel stellt die Kanne ab. „Die Signalki: Mabel sets the pot down. "The signal children. At night they run to the Signal Slope and stand on the rails. They say a voice promises them a train going up. Like yours."
Am Signalhang steht ein Signal auf Fahrt: On the Signal Slope a signal stands at clear although no train is coming. The voice inside it is thin and greedy. You pull the signal to stop with your bare hand and hold it until the voice gives up. The children go home. One waves.

From the fog by the anchor steps a woman in a grey veil, and behind her twenty more. "You scattered my sisters to every wind. Each of them has stolen a face since. Today we give them all back to you."
Nicht alle Grauspäher halten sich an den: Not every Grey Scout follows the decree. A dozen wait in the Office of Light, their lamps turned to full flame. "The file is closed," says their leader. "We are not."
Die Wärter des alten Leuchtfeuers haben: The keepers of the old Beacon have gathered what remained after it went out: embers, prayers, hatred. Now it burns in them. "You put out our light. We'll show you what it feels like to stand in the dark."
Die Wärter des Leuchtfeuers haben dich n: The keepers of the Beacon never forgot you: the stranger who escaped them across the sea. Brandt has sent them, with embers in their hands and names on their lips. "The fire didn't get you back then. Today we make up for what it missed."
Die Wärter des Leuchtfeuers knien nicht: The keepers of the Beacon no longer kneel before you. They have bottled the fire in lanterns and convinced themselves it obeys them and not you. "A Light Master who runs away is no Light Master. We're taking the fire back."
Fünf Kopfgeldjäger, die das Kopfgeld auf: Five bounty hunters who never took down the bounty on you. By now it is high enough to die for. "Demigod or not," says one, reloading, "paid is paid."
You defeated the Old One's Conductor. His brakemen buried him under the turntable and have waited ever since. Their faces are sooted, their eyes as empty as tunnels. "The Old One has forgotten nothing. Neither have we."
Nicht alle haben vergessen, was du ihnen: Not everyone has forgotten what you did to them. In every old city there are people who want revenge.
